emma: Hey folks — customer-facing stream (/v1/streams) is dropping mid-response for long outputs (>2k tokens). They see partial JSON chunks then the connection dies. Started after today's 08:12 deploy. Ticket #1234. Any ideas?

jules: Can you paste the server logs + a minimal repro (curl or Node)? Also, is the client using a proxy or special auth header? Could be auth/billing retries too.

emma: Repro attached, here's the key bits: curl --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.test/v1/streams -d @prompt.json  # output stream
Server log tail: 
```
ERROR [runtime] conn=0x7f8a3b send() returned -1: EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)
ERROR [runtime] conn=0x7f8a3b write failed after 3 retries: aborting stream
INFO [http] conn=0x7f8a3b client closed connection
```
Client sees partial chunk (truncated JSON) then socket closed. Also noticed a flurry of reconnects triggers some 401s — corporate proxy sometimes strips Authorization on reconnect, causing extra auth failures and billing spikes for retries.

jules: Thanks. Can you confirm if the client is pausing reads (e.g., slow consumer) or if network is dropping? If you can reproduce, dump the exact request headers and the approximate pause duration.

emma: Yes reproducible: if the client purposely stalls reading for ~7s then resumes we hit it every time. My simple Node repro: 
```
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource(url, {headers: {Authorization: 'Bearer ...'}});
es.onmessage = (m) => { /* simulate slow processing */ setTimeout(() => { /* process */ }, 7000); };
```
Also tried: curl --limit-rate 1k https://... which triggers same behavior. We also observed intermittent 401s right after the reconnect.

matt: Initial theory: this looks like backpressure from a slow consumer. When the client stops reading, the kernel send buffer fills, subsequent send() returns EAGAIN. Our runtime currently treats repeated EAGAIN as fatal for streaming sockets (after 3 retries we abort to avoid head-of-line blocking). That explains the partial chunk then close. We need to change to a soft-backoff for SSE endpoints and allow a short queued window rather than aborting immediately. Can you paste the exact server log lines with connection id? Need conn id to correlate with metrics.

kevin: Seen something similar on canary last month. Workaround at proxy layer: disable buffering for SSE routes (nginx: proxy_buffering off;) and increase proxy_busy_buffers_size/proxy_buffers to avoid proxy-level backpressure. Also kernel tunables matter: consider bumping net.ipv4.tcp_wmem and net.core.wmem_max on boxes serving high-sse traffic.

emma: Here's the exact minimal repro steps I ran: 1) open EventSource, 2) wait 3 messages, 3) in handler block for 7s, 4) observe send EAGAIN then close. Sample headers we see on reconnect: Authorization header missing sometimes (corp-proxy bug). So two issues interact: slow client causing server write stall, and proxy stripping auth on reconnect leading to 401s and extra reconnect storms.

matt: Action items: (1) Eng-runtime will ship a canary patch to treat EAGAIN on streaming sockets as non-fatal for a 2s grace period and perform exponential backoff flushes. (2) SRE to canary nginx config with proxy_buffering off for /v1/streams. (3) Support to advise customer to increase client read window or use chunked processing to avoid 7s stalls and recommend sticky tokens to their proxy team.

kevin: I'll roll the nginx change to 10% of stream servers in prod canary. Command snippet: 
```
location /v1/streams {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_buffers 8 16k;
  proxy_busy_buffers_size 32k;
}
```
Note: watch memory footprint. Also recommend sysctl tweaks: 
```
echo 4194304 > /proc/sys/net/core/wmem_max
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_wmem=4096 87380 4194304
```

jules: Assigned P1 to eng-runtime (matt) and SRE (kevin). Support will contact customer with repro mitigation steps and a temporary workaround (client-side chunking + token sticky workaround). ETA: canary patch within 4h, nginx canary in 1h. Thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy job #deploy-2026-08-18-0812 started to canary pool.
